meta.title: Natural Vegetation and Wildlife
meta.intro: Class 9 Geography study notes: Natural Vegetation and Wildlife.

objectives: Explain the controls of natural vegetation.
Identify threats to wildlife and conservation measures.

blocks.text: Natural vegetation consists of plant communities that grow naturally with limited direct human interference. Temperature, moisture, photoperiod, soil and relief affect its distribution.
Altitude creates distinct vegetation belts in mountainous regions; human activity can transform natural habitats.

blocks.title: Remember
blocks.text: Altitude creates distinct vegetation belts in mountainous regions; human activity can transform natural habitats.
Tropical evergreen forests occur in areas of heavy rainfall; tropical deciduous forests shed leaves during the dry season.
Thorn forests occur in arid regions; montane vegetation changes with altitude; mangroves grow in tidal coastal and deltaic areas, including the Sundarbans.

blocks.title: Remember
blocks.text: Thorn forests occur in arid regions; montane vegetation changes with altitude; mangroves grow in tidal coastal and deltaic areas, including the Sundarbans.
India’s varied habitats support mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians, fish and insects. Forests, grasslands, deserts, wetlands, mountains, rivers and coasts each support distinctive species.
Biodiversity includes variation within species, between species and among ecosystems. It supports pollination, food webs, soil health and livelihoods.

blocks.title: Remember
blocks.text: Biodiversity includes variation within species, between species and among ecosystems. It supports pollination, food webs, soil health and livelihoods.
Habitat loss, fragmentation, poaching, pollution, invasive species and climate change threaten biodiversity.
National parks, wildlife sanctuaries, biosphere reserves, habitat restoration, wildlife corridors and community participation support conservation.

revision.summary: Natural vegetation consists of plant communities that grow naturally with limited direct human interference. Temperature, moisture, photoperiod, soil and relief affect its distribution. Altitude creates distinct vegetation belts in mountainous regions; human activity can transform natural habitats. Tropical evergreen forests occur in areas of heavy rainfall; tropical deciduous forests shed leaves during the dry season. Thorn forests occur in arid regions; montane vegetation changes with altitude; mangroves grow in tidal coastal and deltaic areas, including the Sundarbans. India’s varied habitats support mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians, fish and insects. Forests, grasslands, deserts, wetlands, mountains, rivers and coasts each support distinctive species. Biodiversity includes variation within species, between species and among ecosystems. It supports pollination, food webs, soil health and livelihoods. Habitat loss, fragmentation, poaching, pollution, invasive species and climate change threaten biodiversity. National parks, wildlife sanctuaries, biosphere reserves, habitat restoration, wildlife corridors and community participation support conservation.
